segments.text: This is GitHub trending weekly number five and today we'll explore the 19 most trending GitHub repositories making
waves this week from AI and developer tools. Whether you're a coder, researcher, or builder, these repos will
give you something new to clone, learn, and experiment with. Let's dive into this week's trending open source projects.
First up, Common Forms, a project that automatically converts any PDF into a fillable form. This repo introduces a
data set for form field detection, turning document understanding into an object detection problem. The team started with 8 million PDFs, filtered
them down to 55,000 documents covering over 450,000 pages in multiple languages and domains. What's cool is that they
didn't just stop at data. They also released FFDNet, a pair of open-source models that detecting text inputs,
checkboxes, and signature fields with precision.
Next up, meet tiny recursive models or TRM. Proof that in AI, less really is more. This open source project explores
recursive reasoning with small neural networks. We're talking just 7 million parameters. Yet, it scores 45% on ARC
AGI1 and 8% on ARC AGI 2, outperforming models thousands of times larger. The magic tr doesn't rely on massive data or
billion-dollar GPUs. Instead, it recurses on itself, refining its own answers over multiple reasoning steps. A minimalist approach that's rewriting how
we think about intelligence in small models.
Coming in next, 11 Labs UI, a sleek open- source component library that helps you build audio and agentic applications. Built on top of Shad
CN/UI, this toolkit gives you readyto-use React components from waveforms and voice agents to audio
players and chat orbs. All styled beautifully with Tailwind. You can drop them straight into your Next.JS project
with a single CLI command and instantly start creating multimodal. Whether you're building a voice enabled app, a real-time transcription tool, or a chat
agent with sound, 11Labs UI saves you hours of design and setup.
Next on our list is Dexter, an open-source financial agent in just about 200 lines of code. Imagine clawed code, but built specifically for
financial analysis. Dexter plans tasks, runs autonomously, validates its own work, and even researches stocks, all
using real-time market data. It's powered by open tools like Langchain for managing LLM, prompts, and outputs. And the best part, you don't need coding
experience to get started. Under the hood, Dexter breaks complex financial questions into step-by-step research
plans, executes them, and refineses the results until it's confident in its findings.
Next up, firm. A new way to manage work where your entire business is treated as code. Think of it as a textbased work
management system for technologists. One that replaces scattered SAS tools with simple version controlled text files you
actually own. With Firm, your business becomes a graph. Customers link to projects, projects linked to tasks, and
people connect to organizations. All defined in a lightweight DSL stored locally on your machine. It's open, customizable, and automation friendly.
You can search it, report from it, or plug in AI tools that read and write directly to your business structure.
Meet Full Stack Agent, an AI powered full stack development platform that lets you build and deploy web apps with
natural language. Powered by clawed code and Kubernetes, it turns your ideas into working applications, all from simple
text commands. Each project spins up its own isolated sandbox complete with automatic postgresql provisioning,
GitHub integration, and even a built-in web terminal so you can interact directly with your environment. Think of it as your AI powered full stack
assistant. Code, deploy, and iterate all from one intelligent command line.
All right, here's one that's guaranteed to stir up some drama. It's called What's That? a brutally honest WhatsApp
web analyzer that exposes the hidden politics in your group chats. This Chrome extension quietly tracks reactions and replies to reveal the
social gravity you feel but can't quite prove, like who gets ignored, who secretly runs the chat, and who just thinks they do. It surfaces relationship
maps, influence scores, and bias patterns, all locally stored. Nothing leaves your machine. You'll see who
reacts to whom, when people actually pay attention, and which members have formed reaction cartels.
Next up, Bento PDF, a privacy first clientside PDF toolkit that lets you edit, merge, split, and process PDF files directly in your browser.
Everything happens on your machine. No servers, no limits, no waiting. You can merge, split, rotate, extract, or reorder pages with drag and drop
simplicity. It even includes editing tools for adding watermarks, headers, signatures, or running OCR. All built using modern web tech for lightning fast
performance. Whether you're securing a document, compressing it, or converting markdowns straight to PDF, Bento PDF gives you full control. Totally free and open source.
Let's talk about Neura Hustle Tracker, a cross-platform productivity tracker that watches what you actually do, not what
you think you're doing. Built entirely in Rust with a slick Ratatouille terminal dashboard, it logs every app you touch from VS Code to Chrome and
shows your day as a visual timeline of focus, distraction, and deep work. It's local first, stores data in Postgress
SQL and refreshes every 5 seconds so your hustle stats are always live.
You'll see who your real-time thief is, Slack, Spotify, or Stack Overflow.
Meet Puff and Thinking, a multimodal model that integrates camera geometry directly into its neural reasoning. This
model doesn't just process images. It understands focal length, field of view, perspective, and even the intent behind a shot. It runs what the researchers
call thinking with camera, decoupling geometric context, predicting parameters, and linking visual cues to
real world photographic principles. The secret behind it, the Puffin 4M data set. 4 million vision language camera
triplets that teach AI spatial imagination and cross view reasoning.
If you've ever lost track of your scheduled jobs, meet your command line best friend, Crawboard. Crawboard is a terminal based application that gives
you a clean, human readable view of all your cron jobs, both local and remote.
It's built for system administrators, DevOps engineers, and anyone who lives inside a terminal window. With Crawboard, you can add, edit, pause, or
delete cron jobs in seconds. No more manually editing cron tabs and hoping you don't break syntax. It connects securely via SSH, supports both password
and key authentication, and even shows last and next runtimes in a beautifully formatted way.
Ever noticed how search results often look exactly the same at the top? Enter Pyiversity, a lightweight Python library designed to make retrieval results more diverse without losing relevance.
Pyiversity implements popular strategies like MMR, MSD, DPP, and cover to efficiently rerank results, ensuring you
get items that are both relevant and varied. The API is simple, fast, and only depends on NumPy. So even thousands
of results can be diversified in milliseconds. Whether it's e-commerce, news search, academic retrieval, or feeding LLMs with non-redundant
passages, Pyiversity helps you explore more and repeat less.
Imagine an AI that doesn't just chat about tasks, it uses your computer to get them done. That's open computer use, an open- source platform for autonomous
AI agents with computer control. These agents can browse the web like humans, searching, clicking, filling forms, and
extracting data. Run terminal commands, manage files, and execute scripts.
Control desktop applications with full UI automation. Windows, mouse, keyboard, and even screenshots. With a multi-agent
orchestration system, complex workflows are broken into smaller tasks, executed sequentially, and reported back in real time.
Next up is Blaze, a tiny hackable full text search engine built for hackers, not hyperscalers. Blaze implements
inverted indexing, boolean queries, phrase search, proximity ranking, and BM25 scoring, all in a small,
understandable Go code base. If you've ever wondered how search engines work under the hood, Blaze lets you explore tokenization, stemming, stop word
filtering, and index structures, all without the overhead of massive systems.
It's thread safe, fast, and serializable, making it perfect for learning, prototyping, or building smallcale search apps.
Meet Kier, a one-handed, fully customizable keyboard that lets you type with minimal finger movement, freeing your other hand to sip tea or do
literally anything else. Using just 10 mechanical keys, Kier supports hundreds of chords, arpeggios, and multi-layer
shortcuts. Enough to type efficiently, even if you lose a finger. The magic is in its DIY moldable design. You build a
metal wire skeleton, cover it with modeling clay, attach key switches, and flash the firmware. The end result is a keyboard that literally fits your hand.
And if you're feeling adventurous, Kier can even be paired with smart glasses or sensors to control your computer without touching it.
Meet everywhere. An interactive AI tool that understands your screen context without any screenshots, copy pasting, or switching apps. Need help with an
error message? Just invoke everywhere next to it and ask, "What is this error?
How do I fix it instantly? It interprets the message and guides you to a solution. Reading a long technical article?
Highlight the text and request a three-point summary. Everywhere delivers concise, relevant insights in seconds.
Encounter foreign language text.
Translate it instantly without leaving your window. Writing an email but unsure of the tone? Everywhere can refine it into polished communication with a single shortcut.
Next up, Mina Rich Editor. A blockbased rich text editor built with Tailwind.
Created by Mina Massud, a 22-year-old developer. This editor is lightweight and customizable.
introduces fullfeatured table support with spreadsheet-like capabilities. Drag to reorder rows and columns, resize cells. The editor's enhanced drag and
drop system brings intelligent drop zones, block swapping, and error-free movements, making layout manipulation incredibly fluid. Under the hood, it's
built on semantic HTML structures, TypeScript types, and state management, proving that developer experience can be as refined as user experience.
What if your AI could make movies that never end? Meet Stable Video Infinity, an open-source framework that can
generate videos of any length with smooth transitions, story continuity, and temporal consistency that looks straight out of a professional studio.
Instead of a single static prompt, SVI uses a prompt stream, a sequence of evolving text inputs to control how each short clip transitions into the next.
That means you can literally script a story scene by scene using text. Want a 5-second action scene, then a sunset dialogue, then a chase through a neon
city? Just describe it. SVI will seamlessly stitch it together end to end.
Next up, Sora MCP server. A bridge between OpenAI's Sora 2 video generation API and your favorite MCP clients like
Claude or Cursor. With this server, you can generate, remix, and manage AI generated videos all from your development environment. It supports
both STIO and HTTP transports, meaning you can run it locally with Claw Desktop or connect remotely for full multiclient
access. Need a video of a Calico cat playing piano on stage? Just send a prompt and Sora MCP handles the rest.
Generation, status tracking, remixing, even downloading your final video.
